excerpt: Luko was a French neo-insurer for home insurance. After financial trouble in 2023, Allianz Direct bought its business for €4.3M in 2024; it now runs as Luko by Allianz Direct.
content:
Luko was a French insurtech founded in 2018 by Raphaël Vullierme and Benoît Bourdel. It sold home insurance online in France. TechCrunch reported that it had raised €72 million since its creation and sold some 230,000 policies, mostly digital home insurance in France.

Financial trouble and sale

Luko ran into difficulty in 2023 after a planned Series C fell through. Its holding company, Demain ES, entered accelerated safeguard proceedings in June 2023 to deal with about €45 million of debt. The UK insurer Admiral agreed to buy Luko but backed out in October 2023, and the business then went through a court-supervised process in which several insurers bid. In January 2024 Allianz Direct, the digital-first subsidiary of Allianz, won approval to take over Luko's French home insurance business for €4.3 million (around $4.65 million), TechCrunch reported, taking on all 112 staff of the entities covered, Demain ES and Luko Cover. Allianz Direct said it planned to invest a further €25 million and keep using the Luko brand.

Luko today

The Luko website now operates as Luko by Allianz Direct, an online insurer offering home, car and travel insurance in France, with sign-up in a couple of minutes, according to the site.

Pricing

Premiums depend on the property, the cover chosen and the customer, so Luko by Allianz Direct quotes online rather than publishing fixed prices.

Who it suits

Luko by Allianz Direct suits people living in France who want to buy and manage home, car or travel insurance online. It is not available outside France.

This page is based on TechCrunch and Sifted reporting on Luko's sale and on the Luko by Allianz Direct website (checked 15 October 2026).
